messages.content: Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.  Discuss how likely the predictions below are.  • Privacy will become a thing of the past. • By the early 2030s, we will be able to copy human consciousness to a computer. • Wireless Internet connection will be available anywhere on our planet. • All forms of transport will eventually become electric. • The effects of climate change will be irreversible. • Physical money (coins and notes) won't exist anymore. • Scientists will unlock the genetic secrets that could allow us to live for centuries, maybe forever.

message.content:
privacy will likely decline in digital spaces but survive through encryption, laws, and habits, so the prediction is partially likely, not inevitable privacy
consciousness copying by the early 2030s is very unlikely because we lack a verified map of subjective experience and the compute, biology, and ethics gaps are huge consciousness
wireless Internet everywhere is plausible in many populated regions but not truly everywhere on Earth due to geography, power, cost, and interference, so it is moderately likely in broad terms wireless
transport becoming fully electric is likely for many cars, bikes, and short-range machines, but much harder for aviation, shipping, and heavy freight, so the claim is only partially likely transport
climate effects becoming irreversible is quite likely for some impacts like sea level rise, glacier loss, and ecosystem shifts, though the word irreversible is too broad for all effects climate
money in coins and notes will probably shrink but not vanish for centuries, because cash remains useful in crises, exclusions, and informal economies, making the prediction unlikely in absolute form money
genetic secrets that could enable centuries or immortality are speculative and probably unlikely in the near term, because aging is complex, risks are high, and no current science points to permanent life genetic
